edition.name: Friday edition

presentation.ear_right: Inside: violence in half of school classes, a ban on prosecutors' religious symbols, Tennessee halts executions

edition.note: Built from headlines, RSS descriptions and the Ritzau copy carried in Kristeligt Dagblad's feed, published between 05:30 on Tuesday and 05:30 on Friday Copenhagen time, from 132 feeds at seventeen publishers. Three Financial Times feeds (Life & Arts, Opinion, Work & Careers) failed; the rest polled successfully. Danish outlets decide what is news; international titles are linked where they cover the same story. Nothing else was read.

stories.headline: Defence Command admits soldiers fired as passenger plane crossed Borris
stories.headline_short: Army admits Borris shots coincided with plane
stories.deck: The army chief takes the blame for a wrong timeline but insists his soldiers were firing at drones.
extended: The Defence Command admitted on Thursday evening that soldiers fired 43 shots at Borris firing range in September 2025 while a Norwegian passenger plane was flying over it. It had previously said the shots came after the plane had passed. It maintains that the soldiers fired at drones in a different direction and that their ammunition could not reach the plane.

The shots are now placed between 20:06 and 20:08, based on a video recorded at 20:06 and a TDC record of a call at 20:07:57. The November 2025 report gave 20:20, although the Army Command had put the shots in the earlier window before that report; the new report does not say why.
'We made a mistake there, and I take responsibility for it,' said Peter Boysen, the army chief.
Jeppe Bruus, the defence minister, told TV 2 News that the claim about drones had been substantiated.
DR's defence correspondent found the revised report unusually rich in detail, and a lecturer quoted by Jyllands-Posten says 'it is a bit mysterious'.
standard: The Defence Command admitted on Thursday evening that soldiers fired 43 shots at Borris firing range in September 2025 while a Norwegian passenger plane was flying over it. It had previously said the shots came after the plane had passed. It maintains that the soldiers were firing at drones and could not have hit the plane.
The shots are now placed between 20:06 and 20:08, not at 20:20 as the November 2025 report stated. 'We made a mistake there, and I take responsibility for it,' said Peter Boysen, the army chief.
short: The Defence Command admitted on Thursday that soldiers fired 43 shots at Borris in September 2025 while a passenger plane was overhead. It maintains that they were firing at drones, not at the plane.

callouts.text: We made a mistake there, and I take responsibility for it.

rows.text: A soldier records a video; he judges the shots came just after it
TDC logs a call, judged to have come after the shots
The report puts the shots at 20:20
The Defence Command corrects the window to 20:06 to 20:08

stories.headline: Violence reaches half of school classes as government readies bill for teachers
stories.headline_short: Violence reaches half of school classes
stories.deck: Three in four of the youngest classes have seen it, and the minister promises teachers more power to step in.
standard: More than half of Danish school classes saw violence between pupils during a school year, according to a report by Epinion and Als Research for the education ministry, and the government will soon table a bill giving teachers more scope to intervene physically.
Three quarters of the youngest classes (kindergarten class to third grade) were affected, and the problems are also marked in classes with support needs.
Most of the violence happens outside lessons when play, sport or jokes get out of hand, and only 7 per cent of cases are deliberate and planned.
Magnus Heunicke, the education minister, also wants to be able to remove pupils from the class.
short: More than half of Danish school classes saw violence between pupils during a school year, a report for the education ministry finds, and the government will soon table a bill giving teachers more scope to intervene physically.

callouts.text: The extent of violence in the public schools is, to put it mildly, worrying.

stories.headline: Justice minister moves to ban religious symbols for prosecutors
stories.headline_short: Minister wants prosecutors' religious symbols banned
stories.deck: One prosecutor's headscarf has split the government, while a majority for a ban takes shape in the Folketing.
standard: Prosecutors should face the same ban on religious and political symbols in court that has applied to judges since 2009, Nicolai Wammen, the justice minister, wrote on Thursday in a reply to Ekstra Bladet.
Berlingske reports that a majority for barring prosecutors from wearing headscarves in court is forming in the Folketing, but that the governing parties are split.
The debate began when Zahra Sediqi, a prosecutor in Viborg, wrote on LinkedIn that she was proud to be Denmark's first prosecutor to wear a headscarf.
The Association of Public Prosecutors tells DR it backs her unconditionally and that she has fully complied with the current rules.
short: Nicolai Wammen, the justice minister, wants prosecutors barred from wearing religious and political symbols in court, as judges have been since 2009.

callouts.text: Neither Muslim nor other visible religious symbols must be able to weaken citizens' trust that what takes place in Danish courtrooms is objective.

stories.headline: Tennessee halts executions after condemned woman survives lethal injection
stories.headline_short: Tennessee halts executions after failed injection
stories.deck: Christa Pike is in critical condition after two doses meant to kill her, and her lawyers want her sentence commuted to life.
standard: Christa Pike is in critical condition and receiving life-saving treatment after surviving two injections meant to kill her at a Nashville prison on Wednesday evening, her lawyer says, according to the New York Times.
Bill Lee, Tennessee's governor, has ordered an independent inquiry and halted executions in the state for the rest of the year.
Her lawyers have asked him to commute her sentence to life imprisonment, and Randy Spivey, one of them, calls the situation 'cruel and agonising', according to the New York Times.
The state's protocol prescribes a second set of injections if the first fails, but says nothing of what follows if the second fails too.
short: Christa Pike is in critical condition after surviving two lethal injections in Tennessee on Wednesday, and Bill Lee, the state's governor, has ordered an independent inquiry and halted executions for the rest of the year.

stories.headline: EU clears the way for return centres outside Europe
stories.deck: Only Spain voted no, and Denmark and four allies are now looking for countries willing to take rejected asylum seekers.
standard: EU countries on Thursday adopted the return regulation, which for the first time makes it lawful for member states to set up return centres outside the EU. Only Spain voted against, and because the European Parliament has already backed the regulation, it can soon take effect.

Denmark, Germany, the Netherlands, Austria and Greece want agreements with countries outside the EU so that rejected asylum seekers can be sent there next year. Morten Bødskov, the immigration minister, hopes the first agreement can be reached before the end of this year.
Chiara Catelli of PICUM, an organisation that opposes the centres, said the regulation gives member states 'a free hand to send people to places they do not even know'.
short: EU countries on Thursday adopted a regulation that for the first time makes it lawful to set up return centres outside the EU; Morten Bødskov, the immigration minister, hopes the first agreement can be reached before the end of the year.

stories.headline: Jacob Bundsgaard to chair the pig fourpart
lede: Jacob Bundsgaard, the former mayor of Aarhus, will chair the new pig fourpart, in which seven parties have six months to agree on the future of pig production; he calls it a difficult task.

stories.headline: Britain arrests a British-Iranian man in the RAF Fairford case
lede: British police have arrested a British-Iranian man in London on suspicion of preparing terrorism in the RAF Fairford case; Iran has summoned Britain's ambassador, and Iranian state media call the accusations groundless.

stories.headline: Hegseth doubles the cut in US generals and admirals to 20 per cent
lede: Pete Hegseth, the US defence secretary, has doubled a planned cut in the number of generals and admirals from 10 to 20 per cent, to be completed by the new year.

stories.headline: David Trads becomes editor-in-chief of Bornholms Tidende
lede: David Trads, a former correspondent in the US and Russia, becomes managing director and editor-in-chief of Bornholms Tidende on 1 November.

stories.headline: Denmark lose 2-4 to Portugal in Parken
lede: Denmark lost 2-4 to a Portugal side without Cristiano Ronaldo in Parken on Thursday evening; Brian Riemer, the national coach, says Portugal deserved to win.

stories.headline: Funen woman fined 200,000 kroner over dogs kept in poor conditions
lede: A 59-year-old woman on south Funen has been fined 200,000 kroner for irresponsible treatment of dogs and puppies and may in future own only one dog; inspectors once found 29 dogs at her address.

stories.headline: 188,522 runners enter the lottery for 45,000 half-marathon places
lede: In all, 188,522 runners have entered the lottery for 45,000 places in the 2027 Copenhagen Half Marathon; the first to be drawn hear on 5 October.

stories.headline: Switzerland's glaciers lose a fifth of their ice in five years
lede: A fifth of the ice in Switzerland's glaciers has melted in five years, a Swiss monitoring report finds, and their average thickness has fallen by 2.5 to 4 metres so far this year.

stories.headline: EU countries meet on Friday over fuel prices
lede: EU countries meet on Friday to discuss a coordinated response to rising fuel prices, after the US pressed Europe to release diesel from its reserves.

stories.headline: Finnish police investigate break-ins at MPs' homes
lede: Finnish police are investigating a number of suspected break-ins at MPs' homes; Petteri Orpo, the prime minister, calls the involvement of another state 'very possible'.

stories.headline: Nordic report warns the region risks falling behind the US
lede: A report for the Nordic Council of Ministers, modelled on Mario Draghi's report for the EU, warns that the Nordic countries risk falling behind the US over the next decade if current trends continue.

stories.headline: Man jailed for laundering money that paid an embassy attacker
lede: A 52-year-old Syrian man has been sentenced to one year and nine months in prison and expulsion for laundering 3.4 million kroner, including 30,000 kroner handed to an attacker of Israel's embassy.

stories.headline: Vietnam's president to make a state visit to Denmark
lede: Vietnam's president, To Lam, will make a state visit to Denmark from 19 to 21 October, and King Frederik and Queen Mary will hold a gala dinner at Christiansborg on 19 October.

stories.headline: Netanyahu says the Flydubai co-pilot was radicalised
lede: Benjamin Netanyahu says the Flydubai co-pilot who stabbed the captain had been through Islamist radicalisation; the UAE is investigating possible terrorism, and Israel will decorate four passengers.

stories.headline: Folketing passes the emergency plan for the power grid
lede: A broad Folketing majority on Thursday passed the emergency plan for the overloaded power grid, letting Energinet prioritise its 57-gigawatt connection queue; data centres go to the back.

stories.headline: Majority orders an expert group on administrative courts
lede: A majority outside the four governing parties on Thursday ordered the government to set up an expert group on administrative courts for disputes between citizens and the public sector.

stories.headline: Venstre records its worst Verian poll
lede: Venstre has recorded its worst Verian poll ever, Berlingske's first since the summer, though the blue bloc is much closer to threatening Mette Frederiksen than it was at the election.
